facts.raw_span: A 34-year old African American woman
history of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
treated with 4 cycles of ABVC followed by 3060 cGY at the neck and mediastinum
painless, left upper eyelid mass
previously been excised on 3 separate occasions
painless proptosis
left-sided facial numbness
Histopathology: Revealed a multinodular proliferation of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells demonstrating increased mitotic activity
Immunohistochemistry was positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
Axial T1-weighted fat-saturated postgadolinium MRI shows lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Axial T1-weighted postgadolinium MRI shows tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Next-generation sequencing of the tumor demonstrated a splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the partner and localizer of BRCA2 (PALB2)

concepts.why: The patient's histopathology results showed a multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, which is consistent with a giant cell tumor.
The patient's immunohistochemistry results were positive for CD68, which is a marker for Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The patient's histopathology results showed a multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, which is consistent with Rosai-Dorfman disease.
The patient's histopathology results showed a multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, which is consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease.
The patient's genetic testing results showed a splicing variant in the PALB2 gene, which is associated with an increased risk of BRCA2-associated tumors.
The patient's imaging studies showed a lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit, which is consistent with an orbital inflammatory pseudotumor.
The patient's imaging studies showed a lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit, which is consistent with IgG4-related disease.
The patient's imaging studies showed a lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit, which is consistent with sarcoidosis.
It explains the imaging finding of a tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery.
